issues.issue: 2018 unreported Ward wages 9,994 and NJ state tax refund 354
issues.diagnosis: Receipt is a finding on an undisputed third-party transcript; sec. 111 tax-benefit inclusion of the refund is not modelled and is encoded directly as otherIncome (court: taxpayer neither alleged nor proved no prior tax benefit). Issue statement says 9,993, findings say W-2 9,994; 9,994 used.
issues.snippet: Mr. Morino did not dispute the accuracy of the transcript or his receipt of this income.

issues.issue: Schedule C commissions/fees (6,000; 5,500), car and truck (26,978; 32,190), other expenses (8,920; 5,820), 2018 and 2019
issues.lean: encoded as facts: SE profit 2018 22,769 (as filed -19,129); 2019 24,213 (as filed -19,297)
issues.diagnosis: Substantiation failure (no evidence offered) is a finding, not a computation; disallowed totals 41,898 (2018) and 43,510 (2019) added back to reported Schedule C losses. Note the itemized 'other expenses' on the returns total 15,050 and 11,100; only 8,920 and 5,820 were in dispute.
issues.snippet: At trial Mr. Morino failed to provide any testimony or other evidence to substantiate the claimed deductions.

issues.lean: 8,534 (single assumed: AGI 54,631, taxable 42,631, regular tax 5,317 + SE tax 3,217; as filed tax 0)
issues.diagnosis: Opinion does not state filing status, withholding or the IRS computation; with only the found items Lean is 902 higher. No plausible single/HOH variant of the found facts reproduces 7,632 (HOH gives 7,340). The IRS's own figures are not mutually consistent with one base: 6662 penalty 1,382 implies an underpayment of 6,910 (not 7,632), and the 6651(a)(1) addition 933 = 25% x 3,732 implies 3,900 of timely credits/withholding. Missing findings (status, other return items, withholding), not a framework error.
issues.snippet: determined deficiencies in Mr. Morino's federal income tax of $7,632 and $4,244 for 2018 and 2019

issues.lean: 4,466 (single assumed: AGI 22,502, taxable 10,302, regular tax 1,045 + SE tax 3,421; as filed 0)
issues.diagnosis: Opinion finds only the 2019 Schedule C items; any other 2019 income/adjustments are not stated. 222 gap: e.g. a 2,500 student loan interest deduction (claimed in 2018) would give about 4,204; exact 4,244 needs unstated facts. Not a framework error.
issues.snippet: On that return he reported a business loss of $19,297 from TLT

issues.lean: liable (5 months, 25%, no reasonable cause); 2,134 = 25% x 8,534
issues.diagnosis: Liability matches; amount differs because timely payments (withholding) were not found and the Lean required tax is 8,534. 933 = 25% x 3,732, implying net amount required after timely credits of 3,732 (e.g. 7,632 - 3,900 withholding). Missing finding; lateness and absence of reasonable cause are encoded as found.
issues.snippet: There is no evidence in the record, and Mr. Morino failed to argue, that reasonable cause existed

issues.diagnosis: Liability matches (negligence, written supervisory approval and no reasonable cause encoded as the court found them). Amount follows the deficiency mismatch; also the IRS 1,382 = 20% x 6,910, below its own 7,632 deficiency, so the penalty base was a portion not explained in the opinion (penaltyBase could encode 6,910 if found).
issues.snippet: we hold Mr. Morino liable for the accuracy-related penalties for the years in issue under section 6662(a) and (b)(1)

issues.diagnosis: Liability matches; 849 = 20% x 4,244 (848.8), so the amount gap is entirely the deficiency gap above.

Since this is Mr. Morino's first time proceeding before this Court, we will not impose a penalty now.

notes: Encoded as two cases (2018, 2019) in tcsumm-2024-12.case.json; Lean exit 1. Issue-level holdings (income included, deductions disallowed, 6651 and 6662 liability) all agree; every dollar mismatch traces to facts the opinion does not state (filing status, withholding, 2019 non-Schedule C items, the IRS computation), and the IRS figures themselves imply different bases (6662 base 6,910 vs deficiency 7,632 for 2018; 6651 base 3,732). sfrTax / asFiled.taxableIncome / asFiled.tax not used (return was filed; not in this build's Case.lean when run). No framework gaps found beyond: sec. 111 tax-benefit rule not modelled (encoded as otherIncome), and no expected flag for 6651(a)(1) liability (only the amount 'failureToFile'), so a sustained-addition holding can only be checked by amount.
